note: v1, THE DRONE (first round; Harry, 12 Nov: "get even a drone in place so we can start the playlist and replace it on round 2"). A placeholder so the groove can open to the song: 48 bars, 1:34, 126 bpm, on the home note F. LISTEN FOR: a bowed low F that never moves, its fifth arriving at 0:15, a ride bell on every quarter-note from 0:15 (the pulse: common time, plainly), and two clean-guitar cells ticking over it - five sixteenths long on the left from 0:08, seven on the right from 0:30 - which drift against the bar and against each other and strike together every 35 sixteenths; one open low string of the 8-string at 0:30 and 1:01. Library patches only; nothing here is the new sound family yet (that is being built and measured against the old one now) and none of it is meant to survive round 2 except the home note, the pulse and the two cells. Measured, not heard: -12.0 LUFS, true peak -1.29, left and right within 1 dB in every 8 bars. compscore 85.9 (length 0 by design: the slot is 12-14 minutes).
next: round 2 replaces the drone: the new guitar, bass and kit family (bench running) and the piece's opening sections

note: v2, THE WHOLE PIECE, ROUGH (whole-song round; Harry, 12 Nov: "get the song down so i can start listening to it and then we can refine a great deal over time"). The drone is replaced by all thirteen minutes: 409 bars at 126 bpm, 13:03. WHAT IT IS: one steady pulse in 4/4 that never breaks, and three WHEELS under it - riff cells five, seven and eleven sixteenths long - that start together at bar 1 and keep turning for the whole piece, heard or not. All three meet the bar line again only at bar 386 (5 x 7 x 11 bars later, 12:13): the piece is that wait, and what it lands on is plain common time, a cell eight sixteenths long with the snare on 2 and 4, for the first and only time. On the way two wheels at a time meet on a bar line, and those meetings are the section boundaries (so the form, 35 20 15 7 28 5 30 14 11 10 / 35 / 10 11 14 30 5 28 7 15 20 35 bars, is a palindrome nobody chose); the two that have just met are what the next section is made of. LISTEN FOR: 0:00 one strike of everything, then only clean ticks (five on the left, seven on the right from 0:23, eleven in the middle from 0:42); 1:06 riff A, the five wheel, full band; 1:44 eleven's open chords ringing over it; 2:13 seven bars of the seven wheel nearly alone; 2:26 riff B (seven) with the bass on eleven, and the lead's tune from 2:53 (one note to each turn of the eleven wheel); 3:20 stop-time, sixteen stabs; 3:29 riff C, the eleven wheel, the same shape pulled apart, slow and wide; 4:26 five in the left guitar against seven in the right; 4:53 the lead runs; 5:33 the eye: the ticks alone again, the tune an octave down; 6:40 the weight returns and the sections come back in mirror order, heavier (8:53 the hardest stretch: sixteenth-note kick, a semitone up and back at 9:20); 11:06 the approach, all three wheels at once; 12:13 THE LANDING; 12:43 the last chord rings out over the ticks. A crash marks every bar line where a sounding wheel starts a turn. THE SOUND: the rhythm guitars are the first of the new family, ct-chug-l / ct-chug-r (patches/, sounds.md): the old m8-obzen pair with the engine's white-box amp (triode preamp stages, a push-pull power amp inside a feedback loop driving a speaker), a longer pitch settle on the slack low string, more scrape and sympathetic ring. Measured against two records' guitar stems (tools/riffpunch.py, old pair -> new): Bleed 41.4 -> 67.0, The Faultless 37.8 -> 69.1 (the separators' floor is 67-86); 30 candidates, in ~/.local/state/chirper-zero/c10. A/B on riff A, old rig then new, same notes: http://pocket4:8790/clips/chirper-zero-commontime-rig-old-new-ab.mp3 (full band) and http://pocket4:8790/clips/chirper-zero-commontime-rig-old-new-guitars-only-ab.mp3. Bass, kit, clean guitar and lead are still the old family (bass-fat, obzen-kit-dry, m8-clean, m8-lead-guitar): next. WHAT I MEASURED (I cannot listen): every section's level and left/right (heavy sections -13.3 to -14.6 dBFS rms, the opening -20.9, the eye -20.1; left and right within 0.5 dB except the 7-bar seven break, +1.6 left by design: the right guitar enters four bars late); each track against the mix in three windows (tools/presence.py): the first draft had the cymbals LOUDEST everywhere (2 dB under the mix; now 8.6) and the bass 17 dB under (now 9.4); band shares of the heavy sections against seven records of the genre: inside their range in every band (90-355 Hz 2 dB under their median). -10.0 LUFS, true peak -1.29, no flat-topping. KNOWN ROUGH: the lead in the eye is 9 dB over the ticks (too far forward); the kick is the loudest thing in riff A; the sections differ in which wheels play but not yet enough in style; every fill is the same run; no vocals; nothing has been heard by anyone. compscore 94.46 (the v1 drone 85.9): structure, variety, rhythm, master, length 100; recurrence 68.8 (17 of 21 sections return: too alike). motifs.md, styles.md, sounds.md.
next: the kit and the bass (new family, measured), then the sections' styles: make the mirror half differ from the first, the eye's balance, real fills, the lead's sound

note: v3, THE KIT AND THE BASS (palette round; no note of the piece changed). The new family now has a bass, a kit and a drums bus (patches/ct-bass.yaml, patches/ct-kit.yaml; sounds.md), each set against real records' stems with the old sound beside it. LISTEN FOR: the SNARE - it cracks and is gone (it speaks in 4 ms where the old one took 12, and is over in about 55 ms where the old one rang 140-230) and has a body under the crack; the BASS - a growl under the guitars instead of sub and hiss; the TOMS in every fill - struck skins with a pitch (F C Ab F C), most exposed at 6:36-6:44 into the rebuild; the china, crash and ride are struck plates now. A/B, v2 then v3, same bars: riff A http://pocket4:8790/clips/chirper-zero-commontime-v2-v3-riffA-ab.mp3 ; riff C http://pocket4:8790/clips/chirper-zero-commontime-v2-v3-riffC-ab.mp3 ; the toms and the fill into the rebuild http://pocket4:8790/clips/chirper-zero-commontime-v2-v3-toms-fill-ab.mp3 ; the hardest stretch http://pocket4:8790/clips/chirper-zero-commontime-v2-v3-hardest-ab.mp3. WHAT WAS MEASURED (I cannot listen). SNARE: the engine's physical drum (a stick on two coupled heads, a shell, wires), tightened; tools/drumpunch.py against Bleed's and The Faultless's drum stems, obzen-kit -> this snare with the old cymbals: 44.1 -> 58.7 and 47.1 -> 56.8 (the snare alone 26 -> 67 and 23 -> 40). BASS: 1/3-octave envelope against the two records' bass stems, bass-fat -> ct-bass: mean error 9.4 -> 4.7 dB and 8.4 -> 3.8 dB (their bass lives at 80-1300 Hz; ours was sub and hiss). The white-box amp that made the guitars measured worse on a bass, and a physical kick and an EQ'd kick measured no better than the old kick: none of those is used. NOT SETTLED, for an ear: the same bench reads the kit a little WORSE with the new struck-plate cymbals than with the old ones: as shipped (high-passed, at the old cymbals' level) 56.4 and 55.5 against 58.7 and 56.8, and the difference is in how the kick reads under them, not the snare (at the levels another kit used them, their wash filled the snare's band: 42.5 and 54.4). I kept them on the physical argument; one line (C10T1_KIT, or the kit's c/x/rd entries) puts the old ones back. THE MIX: the kit's four tracks go to one bus that is soft-clipped about 5 dB (as records do to kick and snare peaks). v2's file needed 7 dB of limiting that the groove never applied, so Harry heard punchier drums and quieter guitars than the file; now the file is the raw mix plus 7.4 dB with 1-3 dB of limiting on the biggest hits only (4 dB on the last fill), so the groove plays what a release would. Each track against the mix in riff A (tools/presence.py): guitars -5.3 / -5.6, kick -5.9 (it was the loudest thing in v2), bass -9.0, snare -9.3, cymbals -11.3. The eye: the lead 4 dB further back (it was 9 dB over the ticks; now 5). Heavy sections' band shares stay inside seven records' range; the top octave is now on their dark side (-19 to -21 dB against their median -18). -10.1 LUFS, true peak -1.29, no flat-topping. compscore, seed 0: 94.46 -> 97.67 (recurrence 68.8 -> 86.8, spectrum 97.8 -> 99.2). STILL ROUGH: the sections' styles are too alike, every fill is the same run, the clean guitar and the lead are the old family's. sounds.md, styles.md.
next: the music: make the sections differ in style (the mirror half transformed, not repeated), development inside the long sections, fills that differ; then the clean guitar and the lead

note: v4, THE MUSIC (whole-song round; kept on judgment, the score fell: see the end). v3 had every section's notes as first sketched; this round is about what happens inside the sections and how the piece ends. LISTEN FOR: (1) RIFF A GROWS, 1:06-1:44: every five bars the five wheel lands on a bar line and a second guitar adds the hook notes above the riff - an octave up on the left, then both sides, then an octave and a fifth. http://pocket4:8790/clips/chirper-zero-commontime-v4-riffA-grows.mp3 (2) THE GROUND MOVES. F is still home, but the two seven-bar breaks are on Ab (2:13, 9:46), the lead runs over Db (4:53), and after the eye the weight comes back by fourths, F, Bb (6:59), Eb (7:20), home at 7:46. (3) THE EYE HAS CHORDS, 5:33: Db, Ab, Gb, F under the ticks, changing on the eleven wheel, one to each phrase of the tune so each phrase's held note is a chord tone; the tune twice, low then an octave up. http://pocket4:8790/clips/chirper-zero-commontime-v4-eye-chords.mp3 (4) THE APPROACH AND THE LANDING, 11:06: the band drops to the three ticks alone, as at the start; a heartbeat; then each wheel's guitar enters where that wheel next meets a bar line (seven at 11:20, five at 11:26, eleven with the full band and the tune at 11:31); double time from 11:47; at 12:09 the band STOPS and the three ticks run alone for two bars into the bar line they have been turning towards since bar 1; the landing is four bars of one chord on every bar line over the plainest beat there is, then the common-time riff. http://pocket4:8790/clips/chirper-zero-commontime-v4-approach-landing.mp3 and v3 then v4 at the landing: http://pocket4:8790/clips/chirper-zero-commontime-v3-v4-landing-ab.mp3 (5) the lead's run is a figure that climbs a step each turn of the seven wheel, with one held note every fourth turn, instead of a random walk: http://pocket4:8790/clips/chirper-zero-commontime-v3-v4-solo-ab.mp3 (6) drums: six kinds of fill instead of one; ghost notes in the breaks; the swap (10:00) over a floor-tom pulse with no cymbals http://pocket4:8790/clips/chirper-zero-commontime-v3-v4-tom-pulse-ab.mp3 ; the hardest stretch's last seven bars with the snare on the off-beats http://pocket4:8790/clips/chirper-zero-commontime-v4-hardest-to-offbeats.mp3 ; the hats and the ride can be heard (at the cymbals' fader a closed hat read 27-29 dB under the mix, the ride 23: now 16 and 12-15; the first break, v3 then v4: http://pocket4:8790/clips/chirper-zero-commontime-v3-v4-seven-break-ab.mp3). (7) a noise swell before 1:06, 3:29, 6:40, 6:59 and the landing, and a low drop on each. WHAT I MEASURED (I cannot listen): the approach really does fall and climb - bar by bar -12 dBFS before it, -19 to -22 over its first seven bars, -16 when the first guitar enters, -12 at the full band, -17 and -23 in the two bars before the landing, -13 on it; each new part against the mix where it plays (tools/presence.py): the second guitar 9 dB under in riff A, the lead 6 under in its run, the floor-tom pulse 8 under (a little loud), the swell 11 under. -10.1 LUFS, true peak -1.29, no flat-topping; the groove's raw mix is the file minus 7.4 dB as in v3. NOT HEARD BY ANYONE, and exposed: the eye's chords under the tune; the second guitar's fifths over the hook's tritone; the two bars of ticks alone before the landing. THE SCORE FELL, and I kept it: seeds 0 / 11, v3 97.67 / 99.94 -> v4 94.47 / 95.29. All of it is one term, recurrence (86.8 / 100 -> 67.3 / 72.2): the share of sections that closely match an earlier one went from 0.72 / 0.70, exactly on the term's ceiling of 0.70, to 0.76 / 0.75. Every other term is 100. What moved it, from trials on the way: moving sections to other grounds LOWERED the share (0.70, 99.96 on seed 0), and making the hats and the ride audible RAISED it again (0.75): a section whose cymbals nobody could hear counted as different from the others. I would not make a part inaudible for that. But the term is also right about this piece: its heavy sections are too alike in SOUND - one rhythm rig, one kit, one level - and the next round is that: a second rig for the open chords and riff C, and the clean guitar and lead. motifs.md, styles.md, sounds.md.
next: contrast in SOUND between the heavy sections: a second rig for eleven's open chords and riff C (new names), then the clean guitar and the lead; the floor-tom pulse 2 dB down

note: v5, A SECOND RIG AND THE CLEAN GUITAR (palette round; the notes are v4's except one change in riff C). v4's heavy sections all came out of one pair of guitars. LISTEN FOR: (1) THE WALL RIG, new patches ct-wall-l / ct-wall-r: for chords and slow riffs that are left to ring, where ct-chug is for tight muted riffs. A stiffer string that beats, a looser power amp (8 dB of feedback against 18-20, so it follows the speaker), more sag, thicker cabinets with more room, a slow gate. The two rigs alone on the same chords, tight then wall: http://pocket4:8790/clips/chirper-zero-commontime-rig-chug-wall-ab.mp3 . It plays eleven's open chords wherever they sound (1:44, 7:20, 10:28, the approach), the chord over the bass's break (9:46), every big hit, and RIFF C ITSELF (3:29) and its filled return (6:59): the eleven wheel now has its own sound. v4 then v5: riff C http://pocket4:8790/clips/chirper-zero-commontime-v4-v5-riffC-ab.mp3 ; the chords over riff A's five at 1:44 http://pocket4:8790/clips/chirper-zero-commontime-v4-v5-chords-over-five-ab.mp3 ; the bass's break http://pocket4:8790/clips/chirper-zero-commontime-v4-v5-bass-break-ab.mp3 (2) RIFF C GROWS: its first eleven bars are the riff alone on the wall rig (with bass and drums); the open chords join on the tight rig when the ground moves to Bb at 3:50. (3) THE CLEAN GUITAR, new patch ct-clean, on the three ticks (the opening, the eye, the approach, the ring-out): the old one was a bright pluck in a big room; this is a guitar's direct signal - a neck pickup, a string that beats slowly - through a soft compressor and a clean amp, dry, with the song's delay and hall. Alone, old then new: http://pocket4:8790/clips/chirper-zero-commontime-clean-old-new-ab.mp3 ; in the opening http://pocket4:8790/clips/chirper-zero-commontime-v4-v5-opening-ticks-ab.mp3 ; in the eye http://pocket4:8790/clips/chirper-zero-commontime-v4-v5-eye-ab.mp3 (4) the floor-tom pulse at 10:00 is down a little (it read 8 dB under the mix, now 9). WHAT I MEASURED (I cannot listen): BOTH NEW SOUNDS ARE TONE CHOICES, NOT FITTED - there is no bench for ringing chords or for a clean guitar, so nothing says they are closer to a record, only that they differ in the way meant. The wall rig against the tight rig on the same chords, level matched: 2-5 dB more at 90-355 Hz and 1-2 dB less from 355 Hz to 5.6 kHz; in the song the sections it leads moved the same way (riff C +1.1 dB at 90-355 Hz, -1.9 dB at 1.4-5.6 kHz against v4). The clean guitar against the old one, level matched: 3 dB less at 180-355 Hz, 3.5 dB more at 1.4-2.8 kHz, and DARKER at the very top (2 dB less at 5.6-9 kHz, 13 dB less above 9 kHz: a pickup passes little up there; a version through a cabinet lost 18 dB and was dropped). Against the mix where they play: the wall rig 6 dB under in riff C (the kick is the loudest thing), 9 under as chords over riff A's five; the three ticks 8-9 dB under in the opening and 11 under in the eye, where the lead is on top. Riff C by stretch: -14.6 dBFS alone, -12.9 on Bb, -13.2 home. -10.0 LUFS, true peak -1.39, no flat-topping. compscore seeds 0 / 11: v4 94.47 / 95.29 -> v5 95.67 / 98.71; all of the movement is recurrence (67 / 72 -> 75 / 93), the share of sections that closely match an earlier one 0.76 / 0.75 -> 0.74 / 0.71 against a ceiling of 0.70. That term sits on a cliff here and one trial of this same round read 92.5 / 97.3, so take the direction, not the size. NOT HEARD BY ANYONE, and exposed: the wall rig's low mids under the bass in riff C (3:29-3:50, the riff alone); the clean guitar's darker top in the opening; whether the two rigs read as two guitars or as one guitar with a blanket over it. sounds.md, motifs.md.
next: the lead (a bench-less tone choice too: try lead-tape's voice and the white-box amp on the tune and the run), then the music again: the mirror half's sections against their first-half twins, and the top octave (heavy sections -19 to -22 dB against the records' -18)

note: rebaselined on compscore b9fc8471: v5 (the song file) scores 99.986/99.983 on seeds 0/11; best was 95.67 on an older compscore. Compare candidates against this.

v6, THE HOOK GROWS, AND COINCIDENCES SOUND (whole-song round). FIRST, THE YARDSTICK CHANGED between v5 and v6, at chirp-eco's advice (commit f3869ab4; the scorer's params are the album's to set): the form terms are averaged over seven section cuts instead of riding on one, and the ceiling on "sections that match an earlier one" went from 0.70 to 0.90, because a piece built on one returning motif is meant to recur. Nothing in the music changed for that. v5 reads 99.99 / 99.98 under it (95.67 / 98.71 before); v6 reads 100.00 / 100.00 (96.20 / 100.00 under the old settings). The score is at its ceiling now and says nothing more; what follows is judgment. LISTEN FOR: (1) THE HOOK IS LEARNT A NOTE AT A TIME. The guitars creep in before 1:06 with Ab alone; riff A gains a note at each landing, every five bars: Ab; Ab Gb; Ab Gb B; Ab Gb B C. http://pocket4:8790/clips/chirper-zero-commontime-v6-riffA-hook-grows.mp3 In the last third it has grown to seven notes (Ab Gb B C Eb Db B): riff A's return at 10:28, where a second guitar strikes each hook note as a power chord above the riff (v5 then v6: http://pocket4:8790/clips/chirper-zero-commontime-v5-v6-riffA-home-ab.mp3 ), and the left guitar in the approach. At the landing it is eight, two to a bar: a four-bar phrase, square for the first time. http://pocket4:8790/clips/chirper-zero-commontime-v6-landing-hook.mp3 (2) COINCIDENCES. Wherever two of the three wheels begin a turn on the same sixteenth, a struck bar sounds, one pitch to each pair (five and seven C, five and eleven Ab, seven and eleven F). Only in the quiet places, and only for wheels that are ticking: the opening from 0:29, the eye, the start of the approach and its last two bars, the ring-out. All three sound together only at the first bar line and at the landing. The opening, v5 then v6: http://pocket4:8790/clips/chirper-zero-commontime-v5-v6-opening-chimes-ab.mp3 ; the eye: http://pocket4:8790/clips/chirper-zero-commontime-v6-eye-chimes.mp3 (3) THE LEAD FLOATS, 4:53: instead of a figure locked to the sixteenths, ten phrases that each start on a turn of the seven wheel - a joined flurry of five, seven, ten or more notes in the time of four, six, eight sixteenths, so off the band's grid, landing on one long held note; the flurries lengthen and the last climbs for four turns to a held C. v5 then v6: http://pocket4:8790/clips/chirper-zero-commontime-v5-v6-solo-ab.mp3 (4) GHOST NOTES are the same snare struck softly; before they were the old kit's snare. The first break, v5 then v6: http://pocket4:8790/clips/chirper-zero-commontime-v5-v6-ghosts-ab.mp3 WHAT I MEASURED (I cannot listen): the struck bar against the mix where it plays (tools/presence.py): 11 dB under in the opening and 12 under in the eye, level with the ticks or just under them (my first setting had it 7 and 10 under, louder than the ticks, and I turned it down 5 dB); the eye is 1.1 dB brighter above 5.6 kHz for it. The lead is the loudest part in its run (6 dB under the mix), as before. The power chords at 10:28 are 11 dB under the mix, the tune 7 under. Ghost notes, snare alone after the drums bus: 7-10 dB under the backbeat; a first try at a harder stroke was only 3 dB under (the bus's clip takes 6-7 dB off the backbeat's peak), which would have been a second backbeat, not a ghost. -10.0 LUFS, true peak -1.39, no flat-topping. A CORRECTION to what I said of v4: its ghost notes were on a different snare from the backbeat (the old kit's), which I had not noticed. ALSO FOUND, not changed: the heartbeat kick at the end of the opening (0:51) and the toms that build out of the eye (6:21) are each the loudest thing where they play (3 and 2 dB under the whole mix). That may be right for a build; it is for an ear. NOT HEARD BY ANYONE, and exposed: riff A's first five bars with a one-note hook (plainer than v5's); the struck bar's C over the eye's Gb chord (a tritone); the lead's flurries, which may smear (each note is about a tenth of a second, joined by a 45 ms slide). motifs.md, sounds.md.
next: the score is at its ceiling: rounds are judgment now. Styles: one section in a style the piece does not have yet (candidates: a vocal, the barked voice on the tune's rhythm; a half-time section on the wall rig alone); the lead's tone; the top octave of the heavy sections (-19 to -22 dB against the records' -18)

note: v7, THE MIX AGAINST ELEVEN RECORDS (palette round; no note changed). I measured where the whole mix's energy sits, in nine bands, in three heavy stretches (riff A, all three wheels, the hardest stretch), beside the same measure on eleven Meshuggah records at 0:30-2:30. The records agree with each other within about 1 dB in every band, so it is a firm target. v6 against their median: 3.9 dB TOO MUCH at 250-500 Hz and 1.9 too much at 500 Hz-1 kHz (the boxy range every modern metal record cuts), 2.2 dB TOO LITTLE at 60-120 Hz (our bass's weight sat on its 44 Hz fundamental; the records leave that octave to the kick and put the bass's weight an octave up), 1.7 too little at 4-8 kHz. WHAT CHANGED: the rhythm guitars lose 5 dB at 350 Hz and 2.5 at 750 Hz; the bass loses 7 dB at 44 Hz and 8 at 350 Hz, gains 7.5 dB at 90 Hz and 4 at 1.5 kHz, and is then compressed hard so that its level is the same on every ground (the 90 Hz boost alone made it 6 dB louder on Db and Eb than on F); the drums lose 6 dB at 400 Hz and gain 4 dB at 5.5 kHz; the tune is 2.5 dB lower where it plays over the riffs (it was the loudest part there; its run at 4:53 and the eye are as they were). RESULT: every band within about 1 dB of the records' median (from below 60 Hz to 8-16 kHz: +0.7 -0.6 +0.7 -0.2 -0.6 +0.1 +0.3 +0.5 +1.1 dB). LISTEN FOR, v6 then v7, same loudness: less box and more air around the kit, the bass heard as a note under the guitars and not only felt, cymbals forward. Riff A http://pocket4:8790/clips/chirper-zero-commontime-v6-v7-mix-riffA-ab.mp3 ; all three wheels with the tune (7:46) http://pocket4:8790/clips/chirper-zero-commontime-v6-v7-mix-all-three-ab.mp3 ; the hardest stretch (8:53) http://pocket4:8790/clips/chirper-zero-commontime-v6-v7-mix-hardest-ab.mp3 ; riff C on the wall rig (3:29) http://pocket4:8790/clips/chirper-zero-commontime-v6-v7-mix-riffC-ab.mp3 ; the lead's run over Db (4:53) http://pocket4:8790/clips/chirper-zero-commontime-v6-v7-mix-solo-ab.mp3 ; the landing http://pocket4:8790/clips/chirper-zero-commontime-v6-v7-mix-landing-ab.mp3 WHAT ELSE I MEASURED (I cannot listen): against the mix where they play (tools/presence.py), the bass is 8 dB under in riff A (it was 10), the cymbals 10 under (were 12.5), the tune 8 under at 7:46 (was 6.4, the loudest part; now the kick and the guitars are); in the lead's run the lead is on top (5 under) and the bass 8 under. Every section is 1.5-2.4 dB down at 355 Hz-1.4 kHz and 2-3 dB up above 5.6 kHz against v6. -10.0 LUFS, true peak -1.46, no flat-topping. The groove plays the unmastered mix: it is level with v6's there (-16.7 LUFS in the full sections, with 1 dB of master gain to make up what the cuts took). The score is at its ceiling (100.00 on both seeds) and says nothing; this is kept on the measurement above. CAVEATS: the per-instrument numbers lean on a stem separator; the whole-mix numbers do not. The bass's compressor is strong (8:1); if the bass now sounds flat or pumps, that is where to look. One band I left alone: the lowest note of the drone in the quiet sections (44 Hz) reads 5 dB over the genre's envelope across the whole song; in the heavy stretches the bottom octave is 0.7 over. NOT HEARD BY ANYONE. sounds.md has the recipe; the tool is ~/.local/state/chirper-zero/c10/stembal.py.
next: the music: a style the piece lacks (the barked voice on the tune's rhythm, or a half-time stretch on the wall rig alone); the lead's tone; then fold the bus equalisers into the patches (ct-bass, ct-kit) once an ear has passed them

note: v8, SLOW CHORDS BEFORE THE EYE (section round: the ten bars at 5:14-5:33). Every heavy section so far was a muted riff; the piece had nothing slow and heavy. Before, these bars were riff A fading out. LISTEN FOR: after the lead's run ends at 5:14 there is no riff at all: one big open chord to each turn of the eleven wheel (1.3 seconds each), left to ring, on the wall rig, the bass holding under it, the drums in half time (china on the half-bar, the snare once a bar) for five bars and then only a hat and the five tick coming up.
